Subject: Inquiry: private offer pricing & channel split

Hi Jonas / Ben,

Thanks for taking a look. We're preparing a private offer request and want to understand two things before we schedule a call:

1) Tradeoff between an upfront credit (applied as a negative invoice line over the first 6 months) vs smoothing an equivalent discount into list prices across SKU tiers. Which approach minimizes perceived price volatility for our internal finance team and preserves reseller margins?

2) Novisystems works with a small reseller network — they expect a 10-12% retainer to maintain account coverage. Can Redwood flow a retainer or does this need to be part of our invoicing/partner pass-through?

I've attached our RFP extract with expected usage pattern and preferred renewal cadence.

Attachments: [Attachment: Novi_RFP_2027.pdf (PDF)]

Amanda — thanks for the clear brief and the RFP. High level: both mechanisms can work but they have different operational and channel implications. Quick notes: 

• Upfront credit (negative invoice line): Visible and understandable to finance; good if Novisystems wants a clear upfront concession. Risk: reseller margins look compressed unless you explicitly earmark a pass-through retainer.

• List-price smoothing: Cleaner customer-facing pricing; preserves a steady ARR profile but requires careful mapping of SKU buckets. The reseller retainer needs to be handled via a separate partner credit or reseller invoice — otherwise the reseller will see a lower gross margin.

Given your reseller expectation, two pragmatic options we see:
A) Offer a modest upfront credit to Novisystems and a named reseller retainer (10%) that Redwood invoices and pays to the reseller as a pass-through. Requires ops involvement for pass-through accounting.
B) Smooth the discount into the private offer and provide a quarterly true-up to the reseller (quarterly cash or credit), which keeps monthly invoices flat for Novisystems but needs a clear true-up clause.

I've attached a provisional pricing matrix so you can see the unit economics (RW_provisional_pricing_20270531.xlsx). Happy to get on a 30-min call to pick A vs B.

Best,

Jonas — +1 to Option B as primary. Operational notes from channel math: 

• Smoothing: to keep the reseller at the advertised 10% retainer we need to set a list-price uplift of ~11.5% across the SKU buckets (effectively passing a small portion to the reseller). That preserves gross margin at the reseller level but increases reported ARR slightly.
• Quarterly true-up: easiest to reconcile. Suggest Redwood issues a quarterly credit note to the reseller (statement of account + credit memo) tied to HubSpot deal id.
• If legal won't accept credits, alternate is to route a named payment to the reseller bank account (requires KYC).

I've attached a quick impact model that shows the cash and GAAP flow (channel-impact-sheet.xlsx).

If we run with Option B, ops will need a 2-week lead to configure the private offer SKU mapping and billing rules.

Ben / Jonas — legal check: quarterly credit memos are fine but we need two small contract additions for the private offer:

1) True-up clause: define cadence, metrics (net usage on approved SKUs), and remedies if reseller not eligible for pass-through (e.g., reseller termination).
2) Payment flow appendix: whether Redwood pays reseller directly (requires reseller W9 / W-8 and KYC) or issues a credit against Redwood invoices to Novisystems that the reseller redeems.

For delegated authority: I can sign standard private offer SOWs up to $250k list if Sales records the agreed uplift margin in Salesforce and gets a documented approval email. Anything above that needs Legal counter-sign.

Also include the DocuSign template link when you send the private offer.

Amanda — thanks for the patience while we aligned internally. Based on the RFP and your reseller constraints we propose the following private offer structure (summary):

• Offer structure: list‑price smoothing across the agreed SKUs with a 9% effective customer discount applied via private pricing buckets. This keeps monthly invoices steady.
• Reseller retainer: 10% of net usage to be paid to the named reseller on a quarterly basis as a credit memo from Redwood. Redwood will issue a quarterly credit memo tied to usage (not to exceed the agreed retainer cap).
• True-up cadence: quarterly (30 days after quarter close) with a reconciliation statement.
• Implementation tasks: ops needs 2 weeks to map SKU buckets and configure billing rules; Legal will append the true-up clause to the private offer.
